[p. 301]

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah al-Saffat (The Ranks)

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿By those who range in ranks﴾ ﴿and those who drive away with a driving﴾ ﴿and those who recite the reminder﴾ ﴿Indeed, your God is One﴾ ﴿Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, and Lord of the easts﴾.

Most of the scholars hold that what is meant by al-Saffat (those who range in ranks), al-Zajirat (those who drive away), and al-TalIyat (those who recite) here are the multitudes of angels. The description of the angels as those who range in ranks has come in His saying, Exalted is He, concerning them: ﴿And indeed, we are those who range in ranks﴾ ﴿And indeed, we are those who glorify [Allah]﴾ [al-Saffat: 165-166]. The meaning of their being ranked (saffin) is that they stand in tight rows, side by side, in obedience to Allah, Exalted is He, such as in prayer and other acts. It has also been said that they are called that because they arrange their wings in the sky, awaiting the command of Allah. The first view is supported by the hadith of Hudhayfah, which we mentioned at the beginning of Surat al-Ma'idah, in Sahih Muslim, in which the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "We have been favoured over people in three ways: our rows have been made like the rows of the angels, the whole earth has been made a place of prostration (masjid) for us, and its dust has been made a means of purification (tahur) for us when we cannot find water." This is a sound proof that the angels form rows like the rows of those praying in their prayer. Some verses also indicate that they convey the reminder to the prophets in order to establish proof and give warning through it, such as His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Those who bring the reminder﴾ ﴿as an excuse or a warning﴾ [al-Mulk: 5-6]. So His saying ﴿those who bring the reminder﴾ is like His saying here ﴿those who recite the reminder﴾, because the reminder that they recite, they convey to the prophets, just as Jibril used to descend with the revelation to our Prophet and to other prophets, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon them all. His saying ﴿as an excuse or a warning﴾ means for the sake of establishing proof (i'dhar) and warning (indhar) by that reminder which they recite and convey. I'dhar is cutting off the excuse by delivering the message.

As for indhar (warning), we have already explained it and clarified its types at the beginning of Surat al-A'raf, in the discussion of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Alif, Lam, Mim, Sad﴾ ﴿A Book revealed to you, so let there be no discomfort in your breast about it, that you may warn thereby, and as a reminder for the believers﴾ [al-A'raf: 1-2]. As for His saying in this verse ﴿those who drive away with a driving﴾, the angels drive the clouds. It has also been said that they drive the creatures away from the disobedience of Allah through the reminder that they recite and convey to the prophets.

[p. 302]

Among those who said that al-Saffat, al-Zajirat, and al-TalIyat at the beginning of this noble surah are the multitudes of angels are: Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn Mas'ud, 'Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, and Qatadah, as stated by al-Qurtubi, Ibn Kathir, and others. Ibn Kathir and others who held this view added Masruq, al-Suddi, and al-Rabi' ibn Anas. We have already mentioned that this is the view of most of the scholars.

Some scholars said: al-Saffat in the verse refers to birds that spread their wings in the air. They took as evidence His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Have they not seen the birds above them, spreading and folding their wings? None holds them up except the Most Gracious﴾ [al-Mulk: 19], and His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Have you not seen that Allah is glorified by whoever is in the heavens and the earth, and the birds in flight? Each has known its prayer and its glorification﴾ [al-Nur: 41].

Some scholars said: what is meant by al-Saffat are the assemblies of Muslims who stand in rows in their mosques for prayer, and who stand in rows in their military campaigns when meeting the enemy, as Allah, Exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who fight in His cause in a row, as if they were a solid structure﴾ [al-Saff: 4].

Some scholars also said: what is meant by ﴿those who drive away with a driving﴾ and ﴿those who recite the reminder﴾ are the assemblies of scholars who act upon their knowledge, conveying the verses of Allah to the people, and driving them away from the disobedience of Allah through His verses and admonitions which He revealed to His messengers.

Some said: what is meant by ﴿those who drive away with a driving﴾ are the assemblies of warriors who urge on the horses so that they hasten toward the enemies. The first view is more apparent and has more proponents.

The reason for Allah, Exalted is He, confirming His saying ﴿Indeed, your God is One﴾ with these oaths, and with inna (indeed) and the lam (emphatic particle), is that the disbelievers denied that God is one with intense denial, and they were greatly astonished at this, as Allah, Exalted is He, said about them: ﴿Has he made the gods into one God? Indeed, this is a strange thing﴾ [Sad: 5]. When Allah, Exalted is He, said ﴿Indeed, your God is One﴾, He established the proof for it by His saying ﴿Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, and Lord of the easts﴾. His being the Creator of the heavens and the earth, in which He made the easts and the wests, is a decisive proof that He alone is the one worthy of worship.

This decisive proof which He established here, that He alone is the God worthy of worship, He also established in other places, such as His saying, Exalted is He, in Surat al-Baqarah: ﴿And your God is One God; there is no god but Him, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful﴾ [al-Baqarah: 163]. He established the proof for this by His saying immediately after it, connected to it: (p. 303) ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth, the alternation of night and day, the ships that sail in the sea with what benefits people, the water that Allah sends down from the sky, giving life thereby to the earth after its death, dispersing in it every kind of moving creature, the turning of the winds, and the clouds subjected between the sky and the earth, are signs for a people who reason﴾ [al-Baqarah: 164].

Al-Zamakhshari said in his commentary on this noble verse: If you ask, what is the ruling of the fa (then) when it comes as a conjunction between attributes? I say: either it indicates the sequence of their meanings in existence, as in his saying:

"Alas for Ziyabah, for al-Harith, the one who attacks at dawn, then the one who takes booty, then the one who returns."

It is as if it were said: the one who attacked at dawn, then took booty, then returned. Or it indicates their sequence in degree from some aspects, as in your saying: "Take the best, then the most excellent; do the finest, then the most beautiful." Or it indicates the sequence of the things described: as in His saying: "May Allah have mercy on those who shave their heads, then those who trim them." By these three rules the matter of the conjunctive fa in attributes proceeds.

If you ask: by which of these rules is it in what you are concerned with?

I say: if you make the described one singular, it is for indicating the sequence of the attributes in excellence; and if you make it plural, it is for indicating the sequence of the described ones in it.

The explanation of that is: when you apply these attributes to the angels and make them those who comprise them, their conjunction by fa indicates a sequence of their excellence, either that the excellence belongs to the rows, then to the driving, then to the recitation, or the reverse. Likewise if you mean the scholars and the commanders of the warriors. If you apply the first attribute to one group and the second and third to others, it indicates the sequence of the described ones in excellence, that is: the rows are groups with excellence, the drivers are more excellent, and the reciters are more excellent still, or the reverse. Likewise if you mean by al-Saffat the birds, by al-Zajirat everything that drives away from disobedience, and by al-TalIyat every soul that recites the reminder, the described ones are different. The words of al-Zamakhshari in al-Kashshaf end here.

The one who restricts this (the author) says, may Allah pardon him and forgive him: this statement of the author of al-Kashshaf was quoted from him by Abu Hayyan, al-Qurtubi, and others, and they did not object to it. The apparent view is that it is a statement without verification. What makes this clear is that al-Zamakhshari himself acknowledged that he does not know what he mentioned: whether it is this or the reverse. That is explicit (p. 304) that he was not certain of what he was saying, because whoever affirms something and then permits both contradictory opposites in it shows that he was not certain of what he affirmed.

The more apparent view, which is not burdened by a problem, is that ordering by fa is merely for mere mention-order (tartib dhikri), and using the particle of ordering merely for mention-order, without intending the ordering of the attributes or the described ones, is a well-known Arabic style that occurs in the Qur'an in several places and is common in Arab speech.

Among its examples in the Mighty Qur'an is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿But he has not attempted the steep path﴾ ﴿And what can make you know what the steep path is?﴾ ﴿It is the freeing of a slave﴾ ﴿or feeding on a day of hunger﴾ ﴿an orphan of near relationship﴾ ﴿or a needy person in misery﴾ ﴿then he is among those who believed﴾ [al-Balad: 11-17]. It is not hidden that thumma (then) is a particle of ordering, and that what is ordered by it, which is his being among those who believed, has no ordering relative to what precedes it except mere mention-order. Among this also is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And that this is My path, straight, so follow it, and do not follow other ways, lest they separate you from His way. That He has enjoined upon you, that you may be righteous﴾ ﴿Then We gave Moses the Book, complete upon the one who did good, and a detailed explanation of everything﴾ [al-An'am: 153-154], as it is not hidden that the ordering in it is mention-order.

We have already discussed this in Surat al-Baqarah, in the discussion of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Then proceed from where the people proceed﴾ [al-Baqarah: 199]. Among examples of this in Arab speech is his saying:

"Indeed, whoever led, then his father led, then his grandfather had led before that."

And His saying, Exalted is He, in this noble verse: ﴿and Lord of the easts﴾. He mentioned here only the easts (mashariq) alone, and did not mention the wests (magharib) in this verse.

We have explained in our book "Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab" the reason for the difference in the wording of the verses concerning this. We said there, in the discussion of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And to Allah belong the east and the west﴾ [al-Baqarah: 115], the following: the word "the east and the west" is singular in this noble verse; He made them dual in Surat al-Rahman, in His saying: ﴿Lord of the two easts and Lord of the two wests﴾ [al-Rahman: 17]; He made them plural in Surat Sa'ala Sa'il, in His saying: ﴿So I swear by the Lord of the easts and the wests﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 40]; and He made the easts plural in Surat al-Saffat, in His saying: ﴿Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, and Lord of the easts﴾.

(p. 305) The answer is that His saying here: ﴿And to Allah belong the east and the west﴾ [al-Baqarah: 115] means the genus of east and west, so it applies to every east among the risings of the sun, which are three hundred and sixty, and every west among its settings, which are likewise, as narrated from Ibn 'Abbas and others.

Ibn Jarir said in his commentary on this noble verse, and his words are: The meaning is: to Allah belongs the east from which the sun rises each day, and the west in which it sets each day.

So its interpretation, if that is its meaning, is: to Allah belongs what lies between the two extremes of the east and the two extremes of the west, when the sun rises each day from a place from which it does not rise again until the following year, and likewise its setting. End of his words verbatim.

As for His saying: ﴿Lord of the two easts and Lord of the two wests﴾ [al-Rahman: 17], it means the east of winter and the east of summer, and their wests, as the majority hold. It has been said: the east of the sun and the moon and their wests.

As for His saying: ﴿by the Lord of the easts and the wests﴾, it means the easts of the sun and its wests, as mentioned before. It has been said: the easts of the sun, the moon, and the stars, and their wests. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 37, verse 6:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, We have adorned the nearest heaven with an adornment of the stars﴾ [As-Saffat: 6], and so on.

We have already presented the clarifying verses on this in surah "al-An'am," in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And it is He who placed for you the stars that you may be guided by them﴾ [Al-An'am: 97], and so on. The seven readers other than Ibn 'Amir... [see note below] read this word with the genitive construction, that is, zīnat is annexed to al-kawākib, without tanwin on zīnah, with the bā' of al-kawākib in the genitive (khafḍ).

Ḥamzah and Ḥafs, from 'Āṣim, read zīnatin with tanwin, and al-kawākib in the genitive, taking it as a substitute (badal) for zīnatin.

Abū Bakr, from 'Āṣim, read bi-zīnatin al-kawākiba, with tanwin on zīnatin and al-kawākiba in the accusative. Abū Ḥayyān gave two grammatical analyses (i'rāb) of al-kawākib on the reading with the accusative:

The first: that al-kawākib is a substitute (badal) for as-samā' in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, We have adorned the sky﴾ [As-Saffat: 6].

The second: that it is an object (maf'ūl bihi) of zīnatin, on the basis that it is an indefinite verbal noun (maṣdar munakkar), like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿or feeding on a day of severe hunger, an orphan﴾ [Al-Balad: 14–15], and so on.

(p. 306) In my view, the more apparent analysis is that it is the object of a deleted verb, whose estimate is: "I mean al-kawākib," in accordance with his saying in al-Khulasah (the Alfiyyah of Ibn Mālik):

"And the one that governs it is omitted when it is known, and its omission may be obligatory."

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And as protection from every rebellious devil﴾, up to His saying: ﴿a piercing flame﴾. We have already presented the verses that clarify this in our discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We guarded them from every accursed devil﴾ ﴿except one who steals a hearing﴾, the verse [al-Hijr: 17-18], in Surat al-Hijr.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 37, verse 11:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So ask them: are they harder to create, or those We have created? Indeed We created them from sticky clay.﴾

Mentioned in this noble verse are two of the proofs of the Resurrection (al-ba'th), which we have previously noted are frequently cited in the Great Qur'an as evidence for the Resurrection.

The first is what is meant by His saying: ﴿So ask them: are they harder to create, or those We have created?﴾ For the meaning of "fastaftihim" (ask them for a verdict) is "istakhbirhum" (question them), and the root of its meaning is: seek from them a fatwa (ruling), which is the report of the reality concerning what you ask them about. ﴿Are they harder to create?﴾ meaning: more difficult to bring into existence and originate. ﴿Or those We have created?﴾ from the creatures that are greater and larger than them, namely what has already been mentioned of the angels, expressed by their groups as "al-saffat" (those who range in ranks), "al-zajirat" (those who drive away), "al-taliyat" (those who recite), and the heavens and the earth, the sun and the moon, and the rebellious devils; as all of that is mentioned in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, and Lord of the easts﴾ ﴿Indeed We adorned the nearest heaven with an adornment of the stars﴾ ﴿and as a guard against every rebellious devil﴾ [As-Saffat: 5–7].

The answer to the question mentioned, for which there is no other answer, is that it is said: O our Lord, of the angels, the rebellious jinn, the heavens and the earth, the easts, the wests, and the stars, whom You created, are harder to create than us? For they are great creatures, larger and greater than us. Thereby the decisive proof of His power, exalted and high is He, over the Resurrection after death becomes clear; for it is known by necessity that whoever created the greater and largest, such as the heavens and the earth and what is mentioned with them, is able to create the smaller and least. As He, exalted is He, said: ﴿The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind﴾, meaning: whoever was capable of creating the greater, there is no doubt that He is capable of creating the smaller, such as creating man anew after death. And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Is not He who created the heavens and the earth able to create the like of them? Yes, and He is the Creator, the All-Knowing﴾ [Ya-Sin: 81]. And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Do they not see that Allah, who created the heavens and the earth and was not wearied by their creation, is able to give life to the dead? Yes, indeed He is over all things competent﴾ [Al-Ahqaf: 33]. And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Do they not see that Allah, who created the heavens and the earth, is able to create the like of them?﴾ [Al-Isra: 99]. And He, exalted is He, said in "An-Nazi'at", clarifying the questioning mentioned in this verse of "As-Saffat": ﴿Are you harder to create, or the heaven which He constructed?﴾ ﴿He raised its height and made it proportioned﴾ ﴿And He darkened its night and brought out its morning﴾ ﴿And the earth after that He spread out﴾ ﴿He brought forth from it its water and its pasture﴾ ﴿And the mountains He set firmly﴾ ﴿As enjoyment for you and your cattle﴾ [An-Nazi'at: 27–33].

You have known that the manner of expression with "man" (who), which is for rational beings, in His saying: ﴿or those We have created?﴾, concerning the heavens, the earth and the stars, is the giving of precedence to the rational beings mentioned alongside them, such as the angels, over non-rational beings; and this is a well-known Arabic style.

As for the second proof, it is in His saying: ﴿Indeed We created them from sticky clay﴾; for whoever created them first from clay, and its origin is dust moistened with water, no sensible person doubts His power to create them a second time after they have become dust, since re-creation cannot be conceived to be harder than initial creation. The verses clarifying this meaning are very numerous:

• Such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: He will give them life who originated them the first time﴾ [Ya-Sin: 79],

• and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And it is He who originates creation, then repeats it, and that is easier for Him﴾ [Ar-Rum: 27],

• and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O mankind, if you are in doubt about the Resurrection, then indeed We created you from dust﴾ [Al-Hajj: 5].

We have previously presented the verses clarifying these two proofs and others of the proofs of the Resurrection in Surat al-Baqarah, an-Nahl, al-Hajj, and elsewhere.

His saying, exalted is He, in this noble verse: ﴿from sticky clay﴾. "Al-lazib" is that which clings to the hand, for example, when it touches it; and the expressions of the exegetes concerning it revolve around what we have mentioned. The Arabs use "al-lazib," "al-latib," and "al-lazim" with one meaning. From "al-lazib" is the saying of Ali, may Allah be pleased with him:

Learn, for Allah has increased you in stature, and the morals of goodness, all of them, are clinging to you (lazib).

And the saying of Nabigha Dhubyani:

And they do not reckon good to be without evil after it, nor do they reckon evil to be a lasting blow (darbata lazib).

So his saying "darbata lazib" means: something constant that does not part. From "al-latib" is his saying:

If this is from nabidh (date wine) that I drank, then indeed I have repented of drinking nabidh.

A headache, and a dislocation of the bones, and lassitude, and grief along with a feeling of burning in the belly, are clinging (latib).

The two proofs mentioned for the Resurrection silence the disbelievers with a stone in their denial of the aforementioned Resurrection, by listing them close to it, in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they say: This is nothing but manifest magic﴾ ﴿When we have died and become dust and bones, shall we indeed be resurrected?﴾ ﴿And our forefathers of old?﴾ ﴿Say: Yes, and you will be humbled﴾ ﴿It will be but one shout, and at once they will be looking﴾ [As-Saffat: 15–19].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 37, verse 12:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Nay, you marvel, while they mock﴾. The majority of the Seven Readers, other than Hamzah and al-Kisa'i, read this word as ʿajibta with an open tā', which is the tā' of address, the one addressed being the Prophet (ﷺ). Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read it as bal ʿajibtu, with a damma on the tā', which is the tā' of the speaker, namely Allah, exalted is He and high is He.

We have already mentioned, in our introduction to this blessed book, that the two differing readings are to be given the ruling of two verses.

By this you know that, on the reading of Hamzah and al-Kisa'i, this noble verse affirms marvel (ʿajab) for Allah, may He be exalted, and so it is, on this reading, one of the verses of the divine attributes.

We have already clarified the path of truth, which is the doctrine of the Salaf (the early pious predecessors) regarding the verses and hadiths on the attributes, in surat al-A'raf, in our discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Then He istawa over the Throne﴾ [al-A'raf: 54], and that suffices here so that it need not be repeated.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And they will say, "Woe to us! This is the Day of Recompense."﴾ ﴿"This is the Day of Judgment, which you used to deny."﴾ We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surah Ar-Rum, in the discussion of His saying: ﴿And those who were given knowledge and faith will say, "You have indeed remained, according to the Decree of Allah, until the Day of Resurrection. So this is the Day of Resurrection."﴾ and the verse [Ar-Rum: 56].

(p-309) His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Gather those who did wrong, and their spouses, and what they used to worship besides Allah, and guide them to the path of the Blazing Fire﴾. The intended meaning of "those who did wrong" is the disbelievers, as His saying after it indicates: ﴿and what they used to worship besides Allah﴾.

We have already mentioned that wrongdoing (zulm) is applied to polytheism (shirk) in several verses:

- His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, polytheism is a great wrong﴾ [Luqman: 13],
- His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the disbelievers are the wrongdoers﴾ [al-Baqarah: 254],
- His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And do not call upon, besides Allah, that which neither benefits you nor harms you. For if you did, then you would be among the wrongdoers﴾ [Yunus: 106].

It is established in Sahih al-Bukhari that "the Prophet ﷺ explained wrongdoing as polytheism in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they did not mix their faith with wrongdoing﴾" [al-An'am: 82].

As for His saying, ﴿and their spouses﴾, the majority of scholars, among them ʿUmar and Ibn ʿAbbas, held that what is meant by it is their counterparts and their likes: the idol-worshipper with the idol-worshipper, the thief with the thief, the adulterer with the adulterer, the Jew with the Jew, the Christian with the Christian, and so on. The application of "spouses" (azwaj) to categories is well known in the Qur'an and in the speech of the Arabs, such as:

- His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And He who created all the pairs﴾, up to the end of the verse [al-Zukhruf: 12],
- His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Glory be to He who created all the pairs, from what the earth grows, and from themselves, and from what they do not know﴾ [Ya-Sin: 36],
- His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then We brought forth thereby pairs of various plants﴾, up to the end of the verse [Ta-Ha: 53],
- His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And do not extend your eyes toward what We have given enjoyment to pairs of them﴾ [al-Hijr: 88],

and other verses besides these.

So His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Gather those who did wrong and their spouses﴾ means: gather the wrongdoers and their likes and counterparts, then guide them to the Fire so that they all enter it. By this you know that the view of whoever said that what is meant by "their spouses" is their wives who share their religion is contrary to the correct position. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and what they used to worship besides Allah﴾ means: gather with the disbelievers the partners they used to worship besides Allah, so that the worshippers and the worshipped all enter the Fire together. This is what He clarified with His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are fuel for Hell; you will be arriving at it. Had these been gods, they would not have arrived at it, but all will abide therein﴾ [al-Anbiya': 98–99].

Allah has also made clear that those who were worshipped besides Allah, such as the prophets, the angels, and the righteous like ʿIsa and ʿUzayr, are excluded from this. This is in (p-310) His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best has preceded from Us are kept far from it﴾ [al-Anbiya': 101], up to His saying: ﴿This is your day, which you were promised﴾ [al-Anbiya': 103]. He alluded to this in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when the son of Maryam is cited as an example, behold, your people turn away from it﴾ ﴿and they say, "Are our gods better, or is he?" They did not give you this except for argument. Rather, they are a quarrelsome people﴾ ﴿He was not but a servant upon whom We bestowed favor﴾, up to the end of the verse [al-Zukhruf: 57–59].

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Those whom they call upon seek means of access to their Lord, [competing as to] which of them would be nearest, hoping for His mercy and fearing His punishment﴾, up to the end of the verse [al-Isra': 57].

As for His saying, exalted is He, in this noble verse: ﴿and guide them﴾, it is from guidance in the general sense, meaning: direct them and show them the way ﴿to the path of the Blazing Fire﴾, meaning: the way to the Fire, so that they may travel it to it. The pronoun in His saying, exalted is He, ﴿guide them﴾, refers to the three: ﴿those who did wrong, and their spouses, and what they used to worship besides Allah﴾.

This verse indicates that guidance (hudá) is used in the sense of directing and pointing out to evil. A parallel in the Qur'an is His saying: ﴿It has been decreed for him that whoever takes him as an ally, he will misguide him and guide him to the punishment of the Blaze﴾ [al-Hajj: 4]. For this reason, there are leaders of evil who are followed in it, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We made them leaders who invite to the Fire﴾, up to the end of the verse [al-Qasas: 41].

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And stop them, for they are to be questioned.﴾ ﴿What is the matter with you that you do not help one another?﴾ We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surat Al-A'raf, in discussing His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So We will surely question those to whom messengers were sent, and We will surely question the messengers﴾ [Al-A'raf: 6]. There we also explained the way of reconciling verses such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the criminals will not be questioned about their sins﴾ [Al-Qasas: 78],

• and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So on that Day no one will be questioned about his sin, neither man nor jinn﴾ [Ar-Rahman: 39], together with His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So by your Lord, We will surely question them all about what they used to do﴾ [Al-Hijr: 92-93],

• and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So We will surely question those to whom messengers were sent﴾, the verse [Al-A'raf: 6].

And His saying here: ﴿And stop them, for they are to be questioned.﴾

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 37, verse 27:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And some of them will turn to others, questioning one another.﴾ We have already presented the verses that clarify this, along with addressing two difficulties in some of the verses related to it, in surah "Qad aflaha al-mu'minun" (Surah 23), in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So when the Trumpet is blown, there will be no kinship among them that Day, nor will they question one another﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 101].

(p-311) His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So the word of our Lord has come into effect against us; indeed, we are going to taste (the punishment)﴾ ﴿So we misled you, for indeed we were misguided ourselves﴾. We have already presented the verses that clarify the meaning of "the word" that came into effect against them in Surat Yasin, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Certainly the word has come into effect upon most of them﴾ [Yasin: 7] and so on; and (we have presented) what He, majestic and exalted, related about them, that they said: when the word that is ﴿I will surely fill Hell with jinn and men all together﴾ [As-Sajdah: 13] came into effect against them, they were misguided, so they misled their followers. For the follower of one who is misguided in his error must himself be misguided like him. He, exalted is He, mentioned this in other than this place, such as His saying, exalted is He, in Surat Al-Qasas: ﴿Those against whom the word has come into effect will say: Our Lord, these are the ones we misled; we misled them just as we ourselves were misguided﴾ [Al-Qasas: 63] and so on. And al-Ighwa' (misleading) means al-Idlal (leading astray).

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 37, verse 33:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, they, that Day, will be sharing in the punishment.﴾ In this noble verse, He, majestic and exalted, mentioned that the misguided and those who misguide others will share in the punishment on the Day of Resurrection. In surah "Az-Zukhruf," He made clear that this sharing will not benefit them at all, in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And it will not benefit you today, since you have wronged, that you, in the punishment, will be sharing [in it].﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 39]. In other places He also made clear that the followers will ask Allah to punish the leaders with a doubled punishment because of their misguiding them, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Until, when they have all gathered therein, the last of them will say of the first of them, "Our Lord, these are the ones who misled us, so give them a double punishment of the Fire." He will say, "For each is double, but you do not know."﴾ [Al-A'raf: 38], and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they will say, "Our Lord, indeed we obeyed our leaders and our elders, and they misled us from the way. Our Lord, give them double the punishment and curse them with a great curse."﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 67-68].

We have already discussed the mutual disputing of the people of the Fire, and, God willing, further clarification of it will come in surah "Sad," in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, that is true: the mutual disputing of the people of the Fire.﴾ [Sad: 64].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 37, verse 34:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, that is how We deal with the criminals.﴾ ﴿Indeed, they, when it was said to them, "There is no deity except Allah," would behave arrogantly.﴾ [As-Saffat: 34-35]

In this noble verse, the Majestic and Exalted has made clear that this punishment which He inflicts upon these punished ones (p-312) mentioned in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, you will taste the painful punishment﴾ [As-Saffat: 38], that is, the painful punishment, and in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So, on that Day, they will be sharing in the punishment﴾ [As-Saffat: 33], is that He does the like of it, of torment and exemplary punishment, to the criminals. "Criminals" is the plural of "mujrim" (one who commits a crime), and a crime (jarimah) is the sin for which its doer deserves severe exemplary punishment. Then He made clear the reason for that punishment, because it is their refusal of the word of monotheism, which is "There is no deity except Allah," when the prophets and their followers asked them to say it in the life of this world. Thus the particle "inna" in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, they, when it was said to them, "There is no deity except Allah," would behave arrogantly﴾, is one of the particles of causation, as is established in the principles (of jurisprudence) in the method of indication (al-iima') and alerting (al-tanbih).

Accordingly, the meaning is: ﴿That is how We deal with the criminals﴾ because, in the life of this world, when it was said to them, ﴿"There is no deity except Allah," they would behave arrogantly﴾, that is, they would be proud to accept it and would not be content to be followers of the messengers.

This meaning which this noble verse indicates, namely that this is the cause of their punishment with the Fire, is indicated by other verses, such as His saying, exalted is He, describing their entry into the Fire: ﴿That is because when Allah alone was invoked, you disbelieved, and when partners were associated with Him, you believed. So judgment belongs to Allah, the Most High, the Greatest﴾ [Ghafir: 12], and His saying, exalted is He, in describing the attributes of the disbelievers, who are the people of the Fire: ﴿And when Allah alone is mentioned, the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter shrink, but when those other than Him are mentioned, they rejoice﴾ [Az-Zumar: 45].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 37, verse 36:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And they say, "Shall we really abandon our gods for a mad poet?"﴾.

We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surat ash-Shu'ara' (The Poets), in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿As for the poets, they are followed by the misguided﴾ [ash-Shu'ara': 224].

**The words of the Most High: ﴿There is no intoxication in it, nor are they drained by it.﴾**

We have already explained its meaning, along with the verses that point to its sense, in Surah al-Ma'idah (The Table Spread), in our discussion of the words of the Most High: ﴿O you who believe, indeed intoxicants, gambling, idols, and divining arrows are but an abomination from the work of Satan, so avoid it that you may be successful﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 90]. Here we have also set out the statements of the scholars (ahl al-'ilm) on the impurity (najasah) of the very substance of worldly wine, as distinct from the wine of the Hereafter, and that this points to the words of the Most High: ﴿And their Lord will give them a pure drink﴾ [al-Insan: 21].

(p-313) His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And with them are those of restrained gaze, with beautiful, wide eyes﴾ ﴿As if they were eggs, well-guarded﴾.

In this noble verse, He, may He be majestic and exalted, mentions three of the attributes of the women of the People of Paradise:

The first: that they are "restrained of gaze" (qāṣirāt al-ṭarf), where ṭarf means the eye. That is, their eyes are restricted to their husbands; they do not look at anyone else, due to the intensity of their contentment and their being satisfied with them.

The second: that they are ʿīn. The ʿīn is the plural of ʿaynāʾ, who is the woman with wide, large eyes, meaning the one with wide-set, beautiful eyes.

The third: that their complexions are white, a whiteness mixed with yellowness, because that is the color of ostrich eggs, to which He compared them. Among what is said regarding this is the saying of Imru' al-Qays in something similar to this:

*Like the virgin of the wild cows, her whiteness tinged with yellow, nourished by the flowing water that is not muddied.*

Because the meaning of his saying, "like the virgin of the wild cows, her whiteness tinged with yellow," is that the complexion of the woman mentioned is like the color of a virgin egg whose whiteness is mixed with yellow. These three attributes mentioned here have been clarified in other places along with other of their beautiful attributes. He explained that they are restrained of gaze toward their husbands in His saying in Surah Ṣād: ﴿And with them are those of restrained gaze, equal in age﴾ [Ṣād: 52]. Being a woman of restrained gaze is one of her beautiful attributes, and this is well known in the speech of the Arabs. Among it is the saying of Imru' al-Qays:

*Among the restrained-gazed women, if a small ant crept over the smooth rock from the dust, its trace would show upon her.*

He mentioned their being ʿīn in His saying regarding them: ﴿And houris, with wide, beautiful eyes﴾ [al-Wāqiʿa: 22]. He mentioned the clarity and whiteness of their complexions in His saying: ﴿As if they were hidden pearls﴾ [al-Wāqiʿa: 23], and His saying: ﴿As if they were rubies and coral﴾ [al-Raḥmān: 58]. Their attributes are many and well known in the Qur'anic verses.

Know that Allah praised them with two kinds of qaṣr (restriction):

One of them: that they are restrained of gaze (qāṣirāt al-ṭarf). The ṭarf is the eye, and it is not made plural or dual, because its origin is a verbal noun, and it does not come in the Qur'an except in the singular, as in His saying: ﴿Their gaze does not return to them, and their hearts are void﴾ [Ibrāhīm: 43], and His saying: ﴿They look with a furtive glance﴾. The meaning of their being ﴿restrained of gaze﴾ is what we have already mentioned: that they do not look at anyone other than their husbands, unlike the women of this world.

The second kind of qaṣr: that they are confined within their tents, not going out of them, as He said to the wives of His Prophet ﷺ: ﴿And stay in your houses﴾ [al-Aḥzāb: 33]. This is in His saying: ﴿Houris, confined in pavilions﴾ [al-Raḥmān: 72]. That a woman be confined in her house, not going out of it, is one of her beautiful attributes, and this is well known in the speech of the Arabs. Among it is his saying:

*Whoever is at war with women, I am at peace with them.*

*When they stumble, they call upon me, and when I stumble, I call upon them.*

*And when they appear at a gathering, their short ones are their beauty.*

His saying "their short ones" means those among them who are confined in their houses and rarely go out, as Kuthayyir ʿAzza clarified in his saying:

*You are the one who made every short woman beloved to me, and the short women do not know of that.*

*I meant the short women of the nuptial chambers, and I did not intend the short-stepped, the worst of women, the wretched ones.*

Al-ḥijāl is the plural of ḥajla, which is the chamber adorned for the bride. So the meaning of "qaṣīrāt al-ḥijāl" is those confined in their chambers. Some have mentioned that a man heard another say: "Al-Aʿshā has excelled in his saying:"

*Fair, long-necked, with polished cheeks, she walks leisurely as a weary, muddy-hoofed beast walks.*

*Her gait is as if from her neighbor's house, like a passing cloud, neither slow nor hasty.*

*She is not like the one whose appearance the neighbors dislike, nor do you see her sneaking about to hide a secret from the neighbor.*

So he said to him: "May Allah fight you! You admire what is not admirable. This described woman goes out and comes in often, and the one who goes out and comes in often has no good in her and no beauty. Why did he not say what Abū Qays ibn al-Aslat said:"

*She is lazy about her neighbors, so they visit her, and she makes excuses for not coming to them, and is excused.*

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 37, verse 62:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Is that better as a welcome, or the tree of zaqqum?﴾ We have already set out its clarification from the Qur'an in surah "al-Furqan," in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say: Is that better, or the Garden of eternity which the righteous have been promised?﴾ [al-Furqan: 15].

(p-315) His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, We made it a trial for the wrongdoers﴾ ﴿Indeed, it is a tree that emerges from the root of Hellfire﴾, and the rest of the verse. We have already explained this in Surat Bani Isra'il, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We did not make the vision which We showed you except as a trial for the people, and [as for] the accursed tree in the Qur'an﴾ [al-Isra': 60].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 37, verse 66:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, they will eat from it and fill their bellies with it.﴾ ﴿Then indeed for them upon it is a mixture of scalding water.﴾ What He, exalted and most high, mentioned in this noble verse, that the disbelievers in the Fire eat from the tree of zaqqum and fill their bellies with it, and they combine with it: ﴿a mixture of scalding water﴾, that is, a mixture of water reaching the utmost degree of heat, has come clarified in other than this place, such as His saying, exalted is He, in "al-Waqi'ah" (The Inevitable): ﴿Then indeed you, O you who are astray and deniers,﴾ ﴿will surely eat from a tree of zaqqum﴾ ﴿and fill your bellies with it﴾ ﴿and drink on top of it from scalding water﴾ ﴿and drink like the drinking of thirsty camels﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 51-52]. And His saying: ﴿like the drinking of thirsty camels﴾. Al-Haym (الهيم) is the plural of ahyam and haya', and it refers to a she-camel afflicted with al-hiyam (الهُيام), which is an intensity of thirst such that the abundance of water does not quench it; so it drinks much water and yet remains in intense thirst. From this is the saying of Ghaylan Dhu al-Rummah:

"So I have become like the thirsty she-camel, whom cool water does not quench, nor does her thirst come to an end."

And His saying, exalted is He, in "al-Waqi'ah": ﴿Then drinking on top of it from the scalding water﴾ ﴿and drinking like the drinking of thirsty camels﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 54-55], indicates that the shawb, that is, the mixture of the scalding water mixed for them with the tree of zaqqum mentioned here in "as-Saffat," is a large quantity of scalding water, not a small one.

Abu 'Abdullah al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir of this verse: ﴿a mixture of scalding water﴾: al-shawb is al-khalt (mixing). Al-shawb and al-shubb are two dialects, like al-faqr and al-fuqr, and the fatha is more well known. Al-Farra' said: "He mixed his food and drink when he mixed them with something that mixes into them, mixing (shawban) and mixture (shiyabatan)," end of quotation from him.

**The Qur'an says:** ﴿Indeed, they found their fathers astray﴾ ﴿so they were hastening in their footsteps﴾. What this noble verse indicates, that the disbelievers to whom our Prophet ﷺ was sent: ﴿they found their fathers﴾, meaning they found them upon disbelief and the worship of idols, ﴿so they were hastening in their footsteps﴾ (p-316), meaning they follow them in that misguidance and disbelief, hastening to it. This is clarified in other places:

• As His saying, exalted is He, about them: ﴿They said, "Rather, we will follow what we found our fathers upon."﴾ [al-Baqarah: 170].

• And His saying about them: ﴿They said, "Sufficient for us is what we found our fathers upon."﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 104].

• And His saying about them: ﴿Indeed, we found our fathers upon a religion, and indeed we are following in their footsteps.﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 23].

• And His saying about them: ﴿You are not but human beings like us. You wish to turn us away from what our fathers used to worship...﴾ to the end of the verse [Ibrahim: 10]. Allah's response to them in the Qur'anic verses is well known:

• As His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Even though their fathers did not reason at all, nor were they guided?﴾ [al-Baqarah: 170].

• And His saying: ﴿Even though their fathers knew nothing, nor were they guided?﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 104].

• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He said, "Even if I brought you better guidance than that upon which you found your fathers?"﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 24].

As for His saying, exalted is He, in this noble verse: ﴿so they were hastening in their footsteps﴾, meaning they are following them and emulating them in disbelief and misguidance, as He, exalted is He, said about them: ﴿And indeed, we are following in their footsteps.﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 23].

As for His saying, exalted is He, in this noble verse: ﴿yuhra'una﴾ (they hasten), we have previously mentioned in Surah "Hud" that the meaning of yuhra'una is that they hasten and run. From this is the saying of Muhalhil:

﻿Then they came hastening, while they were captives, being led by them in spite of the noses (i.e., in humiliation)

"His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And certainly most of the former peoples went astray before them﴾ [al-Saffat: 71]. We have already presented the verses that carry its meaning in Surat Ya-Sin, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Certainly the word has come into effect against most of them, so they do not believe﴾ [Ya-Sin: 7], and in Surat al-An'am, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if you obey most of those on earth, they will mislead you from the way of Allah﴾ [al-An'am: 116], and so on."

Allah says: ﴿And Noah certainly called upon Us, and how excellent were the responders!﴾ ﴿And We delivered him and his family from the great distress.﴾ ﴿And We made his descendants the surviving ones.﴾

Its clarification has already been given through the Qur'anic verses, and its explanation was given in Surat al-Anbiya' (the Prophets), in the discussion of His saying: ﴿And Noah, when he called out before, so We responded to him and delivered him and his family from the great distress﴾ [al-Anbiya': 76].

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿When he said to his father and his people, "What is it that you worship?"﴾ ﴿Is it falsehood, gods other than Allah, that you desire?﴾ [p. 317] We have already explained this at length with many Qur'anic verses in Surah "Maryam," in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And mention in the Book Abraham. Indeed, he was a man of truth and a prophet.﴾ ﴿When he said to his father, "O my father, why do you worship that which does not hear and does not see and does not avail you anything?"﴾ and the verse [Maryam: 41-42].

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And he said, "Indeed, I am going to my Lord; He will guide me."﴾ ﴿"My Lord, grant me [a child] from among the righteous."﴾ ﴿So We gave him good tidings of a forbearing boy.﴾ up to His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice.﴾

Know first that the scholars differed about this boy whom Ibrahim (Abraham) was commanded in a dream to slaughter. It is well known that the dreams of the prophets are revelation. Then, when he set about carrying out the slaughter in obedience to the command, Allah ransomed him with a great sacrifice. Was he Isma'il (Ishmael) or Ishaq (Isaac)? In Surat al-Hijr we promised to clarify this with the Qur'an in Surat as-Saffat, and this is the time for fulfilling that promise.

Know, may Allah grant success to me and to you, that the Mighty Qur'an has indicated in two places that the one who was to be slaughtered is Isma'il, not Ishaq. The first is in as-Saffat, and the second is in Hud.

As for the indication of the verses of as-Saffat, it is very clear from the context of the verses. Its explanation is that He, exalted is He, said about His prophet Ibrahim: ﴿And he said, "Indeed, I am going to my Lord; He will guide me."﴾ ﴿"My Lord, grant me [a child] from among the righteous."﴾ ﴿So We gave him good tidings of a forbearing boy.﴾ ﴿And when he reached with him [the age of] exertion, he said, "O my son, indeed I see in a dream that I [must] slaughter you, so see what you think." He said, "O my father, do as you are commanded. You will find me, if Allah wills, of the steadfast."﴾ ﴿And when they had both submitted and he put him down upon his forehead,﴾ ﴿We called to him, "O Ibrahim,﴾ ﴿you have fulfilled the vision." Indeed, thus do We reward the doers of good.﴾ ﴿Indeed, this was the clear trial.﴾ ﴿And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice.﴾ ﴿And We left for him [a good mention] among the later generations:﴾ ﴿"Peace upon Ibrahim."﴾ ﴿Thus do We reward the doers of good.﴾ [as-Saffat: 99–110]. After that, in a verse coordinating with the first good tidings, He said: ﴿And We gave him good tidings of Ishaq, a prophet from among the righteous.﴾ [as-Saffat: 112]. This indicates that the first good tidings is something other than the good tidings mentioned in the second, because it is not permissible to interpret the Book of Allah as meaning: "So We gave him good tidings of Ishaq." Then, after finishing the story of the slaughter, He says again: ﴿And We gave him good tidings of Ishaq﴾. This is a repetition with no benefit, from which the words of Allah are exalted. It is clear that the boy given the first good tidings, who was ransomed with the great sacrifice, is Isma'il, and that the good tidings of Ishaq were stated by Allah separately after that.

We have explained in Surat an-Nahl, in discussing His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while he is a believer, We will surely cause him to live a good life﴾ and the rest of the verse [an-Nahl: 97], that it is established in the principles [of jurisprudence] that when a text of the Book of Allah or the Sunnah of His Messenger (ﷺ) may be understood both as ta'sis (establishing a new ruling) and ta'kid (emphasizing an existing one), it must be taken as ta'sis, and it is not permissible to take it as ta'kid unless there is a proof that requires recourse to it.

It is known in the Arabic language that coordination (ʿatf) requires difference. Therefore this verse of as-Saffat is a clear proof for the fair-minded person that the one slaughtered is Isma'il, not Ishaq. This is supported by the fact that in all the places where Ishaq is definitely mentioned, he is described with ʿilm (knowledge), not ḥilm (forbearance), whereas this boy who was slaughtered is described with ḥilm, not ʿilm.

As for the second place that indicates this, which we mentioned is in Surat Hud, it is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And his wife was standing, and she laughed; so We gave her good tidings of Ishaq, and after Ishaq, Ya'qub (Jacob).﴾ [Hud: 71]. This is because the messengers of Allah from among the angels gave her good tidings of Ishaq, and that Ishaq would beget Ya'qub. How, then, can it be conceived that Ibrahim would be commanded to slaughter him while he was a child, when he had certain knowledge that he would live until he begot Ya'qub?

So this verse too is a clear proof of what we have mentioned. Therefore, after the indication of these Qur'anic proofs, the fair-minded person should not dispute this. And knowledge is with Allah, exalted is He.

* *

Note

Know that this story of the one to be slaughtered supports one of the two well-known views among the scholars of usul (principles of jurisprudence) regarding the wisdom of taklif (legal obligation): is its purpose only imtithal (obedient compliance), or is it situated between imtithal and ibtila' (trial)? It is clear in this noble verse that the wisdom of Allah's obligating Ibrahim to slaughter his son was not that he would actually carry out that act, since his slaughter was not willed as a decree and destiny. Rather, the wisdom of his being obligated to that was merely ibtila' and testing, to see whether he would resolve to comply with it or not, as He stated in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, this was the clear trial.﴾ ﴿And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice.﴾ [as-Saffat: 106–107]. Thus it becomes clear from this that the verified position is that the wisdom of taklif is situated between imtithal and ibtila'.

The poet of Marāqi as-Su'ud (a versified work on usul) alluded to the aforementioned disagreement with his words:

Obligation, the Watchful One imposed it for compliance; so the one who says it entails real capacity is correct.

Or it is between that and trial, wavering; the condition of capacity for the act is thereby nullified.

By his words "so the one who says it entails real capacity is correct" and "the condition of capacity for the act is thereby nullified," he indicated that the condition of being able to perform the act in taklif is based on the aforementioned disagreement. Whoever says that the wisdom of taklif is only imtithal makes the ability to perform the act a condition of taklif, because there is no imtithal except with the ability to perform the act (p-319). Whoever says that the wisdom is situated between imtithal and ibtila' does not make the ability to perform the act a condition, because the wisdom of ibtila' is realized even without the ability to perform the act, as is not hidden.

Among the branch rulings built on this disagreement: a woman knows by established custom that she will menstruate after midday tomorrow during Ramadan, and then menstruation actually occurs, so she breaks her fast before the menstruation comes. According to the view that the wisdom of taklif is only imtithal, there is no expiation (kaffarah) for her, and she may break her fast, because she knows she cannot comply. But according to the view that the wisdom is sometimes imtithal and sometimes ibtila', she is obligated to make the intention to fast at night, and she may not break the fast except after the menstruation actually comes; if she breaks it before that, she must make expiation. Likewise, one who breaks his fast because of a fever that he knows by custom will strike him tomorrow, this too is based on the aforementioned disagreement.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And among their offspring are those who do good and those who wrong themselves openly﴾. We have already discussed this in Surat al-Baqarah, in the discussion of His saying: ﴿He said, "My covenant does not reach the wrongdoers"﴾ [al-Baqarah: 124].

Allah's words: ﴿And We certainly bestowed Our favour upon Moses and Aaron﴾.

He, Mighty and Exalted is He, mentioned His favour upon the two of them in other than this place, such as His saying in Ta-Ha: ﴿He said, "You have been given your request, O Moses." ﴾ ﴿And We had already bestowed favour upon you another time﴾ [Ta-Ha: 36–37]. This is because among the request he was given was the answering of his supplication for his brother Aaron to be with him in the mission, and it is well known that the prophethood is among the greatest of favours.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 37, verse 115:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And We delivered them and their people from the great distress﴾. His saying "and their people" means the Children of Israel.

The meaning is that He delivered Musa, Harun and their people from the great distress, which was the torment that Pharaoh and his people inflicted upon them, such as slaying their sons and humiliating their women. The manner of their deliverance is explained in the splitting of the sea for them, until they crossed it safely, and the drowning of Pharaoh and his people while they watched.

We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surat al-Baqarah, in the discussion of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And when We parted the sea for you and delivered you and drowned the people of Pharaoh while you were looking on﴾ [al-Baqarah: 50]. We also presented the explanation of "the great distress" in Surat al-Anbiya', in the discussion of His saying, Exalted is He, concerning the story of Nuh: ﴿So We responded to him and delivered him and his family from the great distress﴾ [al-Anbiya': 76].

(p-320) His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We helped them, so they were the victorious﴾. He, majestic and exalted, makes clear that He gave victory to Musa (Moses) and Harun (Aaron) and their people over Fir'awn (Pharaoh) and his troops, ﴿so they were the victorious﴾, that is, while Fir'awn and his troops were the vanquished. This was because Allah destroyed them all by drowning, and rescued Musa and Harun and their people from that destruction, and in this there is a great victory for them over them. Majestic and exalted is He, has made this clear in other places besides this one, such as His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿He said, "We will strengthen your arm with your brother and give you both authority, so they will not reach you. By Our signs, you two and whoever follows you will be the victors"﴾ [al-Qasas: 35], and other verses besides.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 37, verse 117:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We gave them both the Book that makes things clear﴾. Al-Kitab (the Book) is the Tawrah (the Torah), as He mentioned in many verses:

• Like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We certainly gave Musa the Book, so do not be in doubt about meeting him, and We made it a guidance for the Children of Israel﴾,

• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then We gave Musa the Book, complete upon the one who did good, and a detailed explanation of everything﴾ [al-An'am: 154],

• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We certainly gave Musa the Book, that they may be guided﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 49],

• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We certainly gave Musa and Harun the Criterion and a light and a reminder for the God-fearing﴾ [al-Anbiya': 48],

and other verses besides these.

We have already presented some discussion on this in Surat al-Baqarah, in the commentary on His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when We gave Musa the Book and the Criterion﴾, the verse [al-Baqarah: 53].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 37, verse 137:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And indeed, you pass by them in the morning﴾ ﴿and at night. Will you not then use reason?﴾ We have already presented the verses that clarify this in surah "al-Hijr," in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And indeed, it is on a road that remains﴾ [al-Hijr: 76]. And in surah "al-Ma'idah," in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Because of that, We prescribed for the Children of Israel that whoever kills a soul, unless for a soul or for corruption in the land, it is as if he had slain mankind entirely﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 32], and elsewhere.

The commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 37, verse 143:

Allah's words: ﴿Had he not been of those who glorify (Allah),﴾ ﴿he would have remained in its belly until the Day they are resurrected.﴾ The glorification of Yunus (peace be upon him and our Prophet), mentioned in "al-Saffat," is explained in "al-Anbiya'" in Allah's words: ﴿And [mention] Dhu al-Nun, when he went off in anger, thinking that We would not decree (anything) upon him. But he called out within the darknesses, "There is no deity except You; exalted are You. Indeed, I have been of the wrongdoers."﴾ ﴿So We responded to him and saved him from distress. And thus do We save the believers.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 87-88].

(p-321) We have already presented the tafsir and clarification of this verse in the surah of "al-Anbiya'."

The author said in *Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab* (Removing the Appearance of Contradiction from the Verses of the Book):

(p-378) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surat As-Saffat (The Ranks)

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So We cast him onto the open shore while he was sick.﴾

This noble verse explicitly states that Yunus (Jonah) was cast onto the open shore, peace be upon him and upon our Prophet. Another verse has come which gives the impression of the opposite, namely His saying: ﴿Had not a blessing from his Lord reached him, he would have been cast onto the open wasteland, blameworthy.﴾ [al-Qalam: 49], and so on.

The answer is that the negation indicated by the particle of negation, which is *lawla* (the particle meaning "had it not been for," which denotes that a consequence did not occur because of the existence of its condition), applies to the circumstantial clause (*al-jumlah al-haliyyah*, a clause expressing the state in which the action occurred), not to the response of *lawla*.

The meaning, stated clearly, is: "Had not a blessing from his Lord reached him, he would have been cast onto the open wasteland while in the state of being blameworthy. But the blessing of his Lord reached him, so he was cast onto the open wasteland not blameworthy." Thus this circumstance is an essential element (*'umdah*, a required component of the sentence), not a non-essential complement (*fadlah*, an optional component). Or it may be said that what is meant by the *fadlah* is that which is not a pillar of the predication (*rukn fi al-isnad*, a necessary element of the basic structure of the sentence), even if the correctness of the meaning depends on it. A parallel to this is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them in play.﴾ [al-Dukhan: 38], and His saying: ﴿And We did not create the heaven and the earth and what is between them in vain.﴾ [Sad: 27], because the negation in these two verses applies to the circumstance, not to what precedes them.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So they believed, and We let them enjoy [their lives] for a time﴾. What He mentions in this noble verse of the belief of the people of Yunus, and that Allah let them enjoy [their lives] for a time, He also mentions in Surah "Yunus", in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Why was there not a town that believed so that its faith would benefit it, except the people of Yunus? When they believed, We removed from them the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world, and We let them enjoy [their lives] for a time﴾ [Yunus: 98].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 37, verse 149:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So ask them: "Does your Lord have daughters while they have sons?"﴾, up to His saying: ﴿What is wrong with you? How do you judge?﴾. We have already presented, in abundance, the verses that clarify this in surah "an-Nahl" (The Bee), in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they attribute to Allah daughters, glory be to Him, while for themselves they have what they desire﴾, up to His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Evil is what they judge﴾ [An-Nahl: 57–59].

Allah's saying: ﴿And indeed they used to say,﴾ ﴿"If only we had a reminder from the former peoples,﴾ ﴿we would surely have been sincere servants of Allah."﴾ ﴿But they disbelieved in it, so they will soon know.﴾

We have already discussed the verses that have a similar meaning in Surat al-An'am (Surah 6), in the discussion of His saying: ﴿Or [lest] you should say, "If the Book had only been revealed to us, we would have been better guided than them"﴾ [al-An'am: 157], and so on.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 37, verse 171:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And certainly has Our word preceded for Our servants, the messengers. Indeed, they would be the ones given victory.﴾ ﴿And indeed, Our soldiers – they will be the predominant.﴾ This noble verse indicates that the messengers, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon them, and their followers are always victorious over their enemies through proof and clear argument, and whoever among them is commanded to fight (jihad) is also victorious by the sword and the spear. The verses indicating this are numerous, such as:

• His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Allah has decreed, "Indeed I will prevail, I and My messengers."﴾ [Al-Mujadilah: 21],

• His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, We will surely support Our messengers and those who believe in the worldly life and on the Day when the witnesses stand.﴾ [Ghafir: 51],

• His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And it was incumbent upon Us to support the believers.﴾ [Ar-Rum: 47], (p-322)

• His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So their Lord revealed to them, "We will surely destroy the wrongdoers. And We will surely make you inherit the land after them."﴾ [Ibrahim: 13–14].

We have already presented the clarification of this with Qur'anic verses in Surat Al 'Imran, in discussing His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And how many a prophet fought, and with him many religious scholars (ribbiyyun) [fought]...﴾ [Al 'Imran: 146] and the verse. Further clarification of it will come, Allah willing, at the end of Surat Al-Mujadilah.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 37, verse 176:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Then is it Our punishment that they seek to hasten?﴾ ﴿But when it descends upon their courtyard, evil is the morning of those who were warned.﴾ We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surah "al-Ra'd" (Thunder), in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And they ask you to hasten the evil before the good, although exemplary punishments have already passed before them.﴾ [al-Ra'd: 6]. We have also mentioned some of the discussion on this in Surah "Yunus," in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Is it when it has occurred that you will believe in it?﴾ and the rest of the verse [Yunus: 51], and in other places besides that.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 37, verse 181:

His saying, may He be exalted:

﴿And peace be upon the messengers.﴾ ﴿And praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds.﴾ He concluded this noble surah with peace upon His servants, the messengers. There is no doubt that they are among His servants whom He chose, along with His praise of Himself in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾ [al-Saffat: 182], teaching His creation to praise Him with it. What He mentioned here of this great praise of Himself, and peace upon His noble messengers, He mentioned in other places, such as His saying, may He be exalted, in Surat "al-Naml": ﴿Say, "Praise be to Allah, and peace upon His servants whom He has chosen"﴾ and the verse [al-Naml: 59]. Similar to that is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Their call therein will be, "Glory be to You, O Allah," and their greeting therein will be, "Peace," and the last of their call will be, "Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds."﴾ [Yunus: 10].
